requirement.title: 2234 The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.text:
# #2234 The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

summary: The bug: since 3.1.1 the analyzer stops working on types marked `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`. The only production change is in `TypeCollector`, where the same edit appears in two copies of the member-collection code. A member whose key kind doesn't match the other members is now skipped after the mixed-key diagnostic is reported, and a duplicate key no longer calls `Dictionary.Add` a second time, which would throw. That keeps the analyzer from crashing on bad contracts. The diff has no code that checks the SuppressSourceGeneration flag, so it doesn't show why suppressed types stopped being analyzed. The new analyzer tests check that diagnostics are reported for suppressed types, the new execution tests check that a suppressed type gets no generated formatter and still round-trips through the dynamic resolver, and the README gains a section documenting this.

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

steps.title: Nothing that worked before is broken

When a member uses a different key kind (int vs string) from the others, the mixed-key diagnostic is still reported, and that member is now skipped instead of being processed further. The same change appears in both copies of the member-collection code.

If two members share the same int key, only the first is stored. Before, the second `Dictionary.Add` threw an exception, which crashed the analyzer instead of reporting the duplicate. Fixed in both copies.
The same guard applies to duplicate string keys: only the first member with a given string key is stored, so the analyzer doesn't throw.

Test: on suppressed types the analyzer reports duplicate int keys, duplicate string keys and mixed key kinds as MsgPack005 without failing. One more test checks duplicate keys on a normal, non-suppressed type.

Test: on suppressed types the analyzer still reports a member with no key (MsgPack004), a private member without AllowPrivate (MsgPack015), and a member whose type isn't serializable (MsgPack003). The diff contains no code change aimed at these checks; the tests only confirm they fire.
Test: checks that diagnostics which only matter when a formatter is generated (partial class MsgPack011, AOT checks MsgPack016/017) are not reported for a suppressed type.
Execution tests: the generated resolver has no formatter for a suppressed type, and the type still serializes and deserializes correctly through the standard (dynamic) resolver.
README: new section on opting out of source generation. It lists which analyzer checks still apply to suppressed types and which are skipped.
